overview: The Medford School Committee approved middle school trips to New York, voted to fund portable defibrillators for off-campus spring athletic events, and celebrated a $920,000 Safe Routes to School grant for the Brooks School. The committee also reviewed reports on student substance abuse screening and heard pre-budget presentations for health services, foreign languages, and mathematics.

items.title: Routine Business
items.summary: Approved the minutes of March 20, 2017, bills, transfer of funds, and payrolls.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Joe Viglione advocated for expanded public access television and asked for a completion date for the high school media facility.

items.title: Report on SBIRT Program
items.summary: Supervisor of Health Services Toni Wray reported on the district's first state-mandated substance abuse screening, which screened 316 ninth-grade students in January.

items.title: Safe Routes to School Grant Presentation
items.summary: The committee celebrated the award of a $920,000 state grant to the Brooks School for pedestrian, traffic, and sidewalk improvements.

items.title: Middle School New York Field Trips
items.summary: Approved overnight educational trips to New York City for eighth-grade students from both the Andrews and McGlynn middle schools.

items.title: Report and Demonstration on Automated External Defibrillators
items.summary: Following a demonstration by Armstrong Ambulance, the committee voted to immediately fund the acquisition of 16 portable AEDs to comply with new state mandates for off-campus athletic events.

items.title: Pre-Budget Health Services Report
items.summary: Toni Wray detailed rising student medical complexity and requested budget increases to maintain AED units, replace a retiring nurse, and add one full-time nurse.

items.title: Pre-Budget Foreign Language Report
items.summary: Foreign Language Director Rita DiCarlo presented department achievements and requested level operating funding alongside part-time teachers at each middle school to reduce class sizes.

items.title: Pre-Budget Mathematics Report
items.summary: Mathematics Director Carolyn Joy presented curriculum updates, university partnerships, and requested level operational funding with a small textbook line increase.

items.title: Report on Personnel Hiring
items.summary: Accepted and placed on file the personnel hiring report covering September 2016 through March 2017.

items.title: Superintendent and Committee Announcements
items.summary: Superintendent Belson announced upcoming matching fund requests at City Council and rescheduled the next school committee meeting to April 24, 2017, due to Passover.

items.title: Resolutions
items.summary: Adopted condolence resolutions for Stephen Honeycutt, Stephen DeVoe, Frank Loschuto, and State Senator Kenneth Donnelly, and extended congratulations on a staff birth.
